imitation

/im-ih-TAY-shuhn/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Imitation means a copy made from different, usually cheaper materials to stand in for the real or original thing.

The bracelet's stones turned out to be high-quality glass imitations, not the real emeralds the seller had claimed.

Example

When the museum's insurers demanded tighter security, curators quietly swapped the original 400-year-old necklace for a museum-grade imitation crafted from cubic zirconia, storing the genuine piece in an undisclosed vault while visitors admired the convincing fake on display.

The piece on display looks identical to the original but isn't — it's a deliberately crafted substitute, which is exactly what "imitation" names.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

fake: Fake is the plainest, bluntest word for something not genuine, and it usually accuses: a fake ID, a fake smile. Imitation is milder and often honest — imitation leather is labeled as exactly what it is, a stand-in made from cheaper materials rather than a lie.

counterfeit: Counterfeit means copied in order to deceive, almost always illegally — counterfeit bills, counterfeit designer bags. An imitation can be perfectly open about what it is; a counterfeit exists to be mistaken for the original and passed off as the real thing.

reproduction: Reproduction is the neutral, general word for any copy made after the original — a poster reproduction of a painting. Imitation adds the idea of substitution, usually in cheaper materials: an imitation stands in for the real thing rather than simply copying it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

original: the first, genuine version something is copied from

authentic: genuinely real, not a copy or substitute

Where it sits · how carefully the copy is made

knockoff → imitation → replica

knockoff vs. imitation: A knockoff is a cheap, unauthorized copy, made quickly and sold at a lower price — less careful even than an ordinary imitation.

replica vs. imitation: A replica is a carefully made, high-quality reproduction, sometimes authorized by the original creator — far more painstaking than an imitation, which merely stands in for the real thing.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — imit-: to copy (the same root as the verb imitate)

Suffix — -ation: the act or result of

Put it together: Just as "imitate" means "to copy," "imitation" names the result of that act — the copy itself, produced by the same imit- root.

Use the root in a new word: imitator: The talent show's most popular act was an imitator who could reproduce six different singers' voices in under two minutes.

Strength Check

Word Choice

neutral to slightly negative

Imitation is often neutral (an 'imitation leather' couch is simply described honestly), but it can also carry a mildly negative edge when used to point out that something isn't genuine, as in 'a cheap imitation of the real thing.'
